requirement: One rescue charge per guardian per individual combat. Revival in that combat must not refresh the charge. A subsequent dungeon combat is a new combat for this rule.

verifiedCallPaths.conditions: For Combat resurrection with an active animator, the coroutine waits for IDLE or Idle, completes revive movement, calls ResetForCombat, then continues the native continuation.
Initializes each participating player dummy for combat.

verifiedCallPaths.purpose: Subsequent combat with reused player dummies
verifiedCallPaths.conditions: Rebuilds player dummy maps and initializes retained non-fled participants for the next encounter, including dungeon reuse.

findings: ResetForCombat restores native actor flags and is shared by revival and combat initialization; it is not an exclusive new-combat boundary.
Resetting Guardian rescue usage from every ResetForCombat call permits an already-spent rescue charge to refresh on revival.
InitDummyForCombat distinguishes the verified initial/next-combat initialization paths from revival, matching the per-individual-combat requirement.
CharacterDummy.CombatFinished is an individual actor lifecycle method and is also called by Disconnect; it must not globally recharge other guardians in ongoing combat.

EncounterSession.OnEncounterSessionEnd clears client combat and vote state at session teardown. Session teardown alone is insufficient to define per-individual-combat recharge across intermediate dungeon battles.
implementationConsequence: Separate actor reset from combat initialization. Revival may expire active protection but must retain spent rescue usage; initial and subsequent individual combat initialization may reset that guardian's combat state.
liveGates: Spend rescue, kill and revive the same guardian in the same combat, and verify a later lethal hit receives no second rescue.
Verify a new ordinary combat restores one rescue charge.
Verify a subsequent dungeon combat restores one rescue charge while retaining the intended native dummy lifecycle.
Verify all peers agree; source inspection does not establish online behavior.
